title: Finalize a PR
bottom_line: Answer its questions once at the start. Then, unattended, it reviews, security-checks and tests your branch, fixes or files leftovers, and opens the PR.

sections.heading: Run it on the current branch, with optional context and flags

blocks.code: /plan-tools:finalize-pr [optional extra context for the review/PR, e.g. target branch] [--label <name>] [--model <name>]
blocks.caption: Every part is optional. It works on the current branch.

blocks.title: What you can pass
rows: Passed to the code review and the PR, for example the target branch. A review level word (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`) sets the review level. The word "security" forces the security review.
The label on any follow-up issues it opens.
The model every helper runs on.

blocks.title: Where it fits in a typical plan workflow

sections.heading: It needs the GitHub CLI; the other tools are used when present

cards.title: git and GitHub CLI
cards.text: Install `git` and `gh`, signed in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

cards.title: `/code-review` skill
cards.text: Built in. The review step runs only if it is installed; otherwise it is skipped and the report says so.

cards.title: `/security-review` skill
cards.text: Built in. The security step runs only if it is installed; otherwise it is skipped and the report says so.

cards.title: `ui-audit` plugin (optional)
cards.text: From this marketplace. Needed for the screenshot audit after the PR is raised.

cards.title: `ui-change-guard` plugin (optional)
cards.text: From this marketplace. Needed for the designer review, together with the `designer_ui_review` setting.

sections.heading: Every question comes first, so the rest runs without stopping

cards.title: Push and PR go-ahead
cards.text: It shows the branch and base. "No" means every stage up to leftover work still runs, but commits stay local. The PR, UI audit and mark stages are skipped.

points.text: On "No", the report says the branch is ready but not pushed

cards.title: Run the UI audit?
cards.text: Asked only if the `ui-audit` plugin is installed and the change touches UI files since the last audited commit. A yes runs `/ui-audit:capture --unattended` later.

blocks.caption: One round of questions, plus a second only if you choose custom audit settings. Questions already answered by the caller, the arguments or the session are skipped.

blocks.title: The UI audit question
blocks.text: It asks: "Run the UI audit after the PR is raised? It captures screenshots and publishes as a Claude artifact or to Cloudflare Pages." The options are `Yes, config defaults` (recommended), `Yes, choose settings` and `No`. If `.ui-audit/config.json` is missing, the option text says the first run builds the config from defaults and captures every screen.
**UI files** are templates, components, screens, stylesheets, design tokens, front-end JS/TS, and native UI (SwiftUI/UIKit, Compose, Flutter, React Native screens).

blocks.title: Settings asked when you pick "Yes, choose settings"
rows: The platforms enabled in the config
More than one is enabled in the config

blocks.text: When questions cannot be asked, because it runs unattended (for example inside `drain-issues`), it asks nothing, skips the UI audit, and takes push and PR permission from whatever called it.

sections.heading: Then it works through eight stages on its own

steps.title: Code review with fixes
steps.text: Runs `/code-review high --fix` on the branch, or the level your arguments name. It fixes what it can and notes what it left, with reasons such as out of scope, needs a design decision or low confidence.

steps.title: Security review when relevant
steps.text: Runs `/security-review` when the change touches security-relevant code. It fixes and commits every high-confidence finding. It runs after the code review so it sees the final code, and before the tests so its fixes get tested.

steps.title: Test plan
steps.text: Writes a concrete test plan for the changed behaviour, happy path and edge cases. It runs existing tests, adds missing ones, exercises the feature per project conventions (for example with the `run` skill for a UI or app change) and fixes what is broken.

steps.title: User flows
steps.text: If `user-flows.md` exists at the repository root, it runs `/user-flows:update-user-flows` to sync it and commits the result. Without the file, this stage is skipped.

steps.title: Your repository's own steps
steps.text: If `.claude/finalize-pr.md` exists and is not empty, it carries out every step in it, in order, and commits any fixes.

steps.title: Leftover work
steps.text: Small leftovers are fixed. Big ones become one GitHub issue each, through `/plan-tools:write-issue`.

steps.title: Raise the PR
steps.text: Checks everything is committed and pushed, then opens a PR with a title and body summarizing the change. Follow-up issues are listed under "Follow-ups", for example `Follow-up: #<number>`.

steps.title: UI audit, mark, report
steps.text: Runs the UI audit if you said yes, adds a `finalize-pr` commit status ("finalize-pr ran") to the head commit once the PR is raised, the test plan has fully run and no fixes remain, then reports back.

blocks.text: If the branch's commits close an issue (a `Closes #<number>` line from `/plan-tools:impl-issue`), that line is carried into the PR body so GitHub closes the issue on merge.

If the plan the branch implements (the plan file the caller names; else `.planning/SPEC.md` or its archived copy, only when exactly one exists and it matches this branch's changes) has an Assumed decisions section from plan-helper, it is carried into the PR body under an "Assumed decisions" heading, so reviewers see every choice you did not make.
A finished PR gets a `finalize-pr` commit status, and a UI audit gets a `ui-audit` status. Both `finalize-pr` and `monitor-pr` use these statuses.

The full step order is: 0 last finalized commit, 0b upfront questions, 1 code review, 1b security review, 2 test plan, 3 user flows, 3b repo steps, 4 residual work, 5 PR, 6 UI audit, 7 mark, 8 report.

sections.heading: The security review runs only for security-relevant changes

blocks.title: Does the security review run?
blocks.caption: Putting the word "security" in the arguments forces it to run.

blocks.title: Changes that count as security-relevant
items: Auth, sessions or permissions.
Request input: forms, params, bodies, uploads.
DB queries.
Shell or subprocess calls.
File paths.
Outbound HTTP, webhooks or redirects.
Templates that render user data.
Crypto, tokens or secrets.
CORS, CSP or cookie config.
Dependency manifests.

blocks.text: Findings it does not fix are reported with reasons, such as low confidence or needs a design decision, and become leftover work.

sections.heading: Small leftovers get fixed now, big ones become issues

cards.title: Small to medium
cards.text: A contained fix: a few files, no open design decision, roughly under half a day. Fixed one at a time, with tests run and a commit.

points.text: If a fix fails, the item is treated as big

cards.title: Big
cards.text: Needs a design decision, spans several subsystems, or is substantial new work well beyond this PR. One GitHub issue per item, labeled `ai` or your `--label` name.

blocks.text: Leftover items are the findings not fixed and the test-plan gaps not addressed by the code review, the security review, the test plan and your repository's own steps. If there are none, this stage is skipped.

sections.heading: Add your repository's own checks in `.claude/finalize-pr.md`

nodes.label: Your steps
nodes.note: Free-form markdown instructions, carried out in order

blocks.title: Example `.claude/finalize-pr.md`
blocks.code:
1. Run `make lint` and fix what it reports.
2. If `migrations/` changed, check the new migration has a downgrade.

blocks.title: Rules for your steps
items: The PR does not exist yet on a first run, so your steps must not depend on it.
Findings your steps could not fix become leftover work.
On a repeat run, each step is told the range of changes since the last finalize (`$BASE..HEAD`) and decides whether to look only at that or run in full.

blocks.title: Create or edit the file interactively
blocks.caption: It inspects the repository, proposes steps and writes `.claude/finalize-pr.md`.

sections.heading: Running it again only covers what changed since last time

blocks.title: What a run covers
blocks.caption: A marked commit is one an earlier run gave the `finalize-pr` status, on a branch that already has a PR. It uses the newest one.

blocks.title: On a repeat run
items: The code review, the security review and the test plan cover only the changes since the marked commit. The UI audit picks its own scope.
The PR already exists, so it pushes the new commits and updates the PR body, adding new follow-ups, instead of opening a new PR.
A marked commit dropped by a rebase or force-push is never used.

sections.heading: Two optional UI checks wrap around the PR

blocks.title: The plugin's one setting
rows: When `true` and the `ui-change-guard` plugin is installed, `finalize-pr` runs `/ui-change-guard:review-ui-change` before it raises the PR, and labels the PR `ui-risky` if the review still finds a problem.

blocks.text: A default only takes effect after you open the settings dialog and save it once. Until then the setting counts as off. The designer review resolves what it flags first; the PR is labeled `ui-risky` only if the final verdict is still UNSAFE or NEEDS ENGINEER REVIEW.

blocks.title: The UI audit after the PR

before.label: PR raised
before.text: The PR exists. It then runs `/ui-audit:capture --pr <number> --unattended` with the settings you chose.

after.label: Audit added
after.text: It adds or replaces an "UI audit" section in the PR body: the latest audit link, a password line when there is one (private-repo Cloudflare audit), counts (changed, unintended, needs review) and a "History" list, one line per audited commit.

blocks.title: When the audit is skipped
items: Your answer was `No`, or there is no answer: the plugin is missing, the run was unattended with no answer from the caller, or no UI files were found. It is skipped with a one-line note.
If no answer was ever collected and UI files appear only now, it skips and suggests `/ui-audit:capture` in the report.
If the audit could not publish, the PR section says so only when it produced a local `report.md`; otherwise the report mentions it.

sections.heading: You get one report covering every stage and the PR link

items.label: opened or updated
items.note: unless you answered No to push and PR

items.label: covering every stage
items.note: sent in one pass at the end

blocks.title: The report lists
items: What `/code-review --fix` fixed, and what it left, with reasons.
The security review: what it fixed and deferred, or why it was skipped.
The test plan, what passed, what was fixed, and anything it found but did not fix, with the reason.
Whether user flows were synced.
What the repository steps in `.claude/finalize-pr.md` did, or that none exist.
Which leftover items were fixed, and which follow-up issues were opened, with URLs.
The UI audit URL, its password if any, and counts, or why it was skipped.
The PR URL, or that the branch is ready but not pushed (push and PR answer "No").

blocks.text: The `finalize-pr` commit status on the PR is fixed behaviour. A branch rule can require it before merging.

next_action.text: On the branch you want to turn into a PR, run `/plan-tools:finalize-pr` and answer the questions it asks at the start.
next_action.detail: After those answers it runs to the PR without stopping.
